parsed.explanation: Adult visitor faces combined federal and division rules. Federal passport/visa screening is the dominant exposure: document-presentation mismatch can trigger refusal, additional evidence, passport confiscation, stranded travel, and possible lifetime fraud finding; federal custody reports severe abuse. The division has explicit nondiscrimination, open documents, city sanctuary and no listed adult facility ban, which reduces ordinary local and care encounters. These protections cannot offset border, federal facilities, funding or custody. Minors face higher care/school scrutiny. Score sits elevated due severe federal stage with meaningful local mitigation.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal border officers may question appearance/presentation. X markers are unavailable; passports can be blocked/confiscated, travelers stranded. Visa discrepancies trigger additional evidence; suspected misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility, though not automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; limited waivers and ongoing litigation; legal-aid guidance; local IDs are open. None of these overrides federal entry screening or passport-marker rule.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening occurs before division protections; state sanctuary cannot stop federal ports, airlines, or immigration adjudication. Passport/visa regime controls first contact.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labor, beatings, solitary, and severe sexual abuse for transgender detainees. National corrections adopts birth-sex placement and forced psychiatric/medication withdrawal; local arrest examples include men’s ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No federal custody safeguard documented. Division police are constrained by nondiscrimination and sanctuary city, reducing routine local stops, but not federal immigration or corrections custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document mismatch at border can become immigration detention; state protection does not cover cell placement, abuse, or coercion.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order restricts government-funded single-sex facilities to assigned sex; some states criminalize bathroom use and an arrest was reported. Federal buildings and funded venues remain exposed in the division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division has no listed statewide adult facility ban; state nondiscrimination covers public accommodations; largest city mandates gender-neutral public bathrooms and protects employees/contractors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State/city protections cover many local venues; federal facilities/funding and parent rules still control, especially where national money or buildings are involved.

care_services.exposure: National restrictions target minors: care bans/reimbursement limits, funding freezes, investigations, and crisis-service shutdown; records subpoenas raise disclosure. Emergency care can be affected by funding/facility rules.
care_services.protection: Adult gender-affirming care is lawful in division; largest city sanctuary shields care-seekers from outside enforcement and deprioritizes restrictions; local nondiscrimination and open IDs.
care_services.interaction: Care risk depends on age, setting, and whether federal funding/records are implicated; sanctuary city helps local adult care but not federal/minor policy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism language singles out radical pro-transgender ideology; visa cables tag trans cases; official rhetoric frames trans presence as suspicious, increasing discretionary scrutiny.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division human-relations commission investigates and orders remedies; sanctuary city restricts local enforcement; independent legal assessment grades division low-risk for targeting adults.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal rhetoric can justify scrutiny at ports/federal settings; local agencies may shield visitors, but cannot neutralize federal enforcement priorities.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minor travellers face border document doubt plus national school/health hostility; guardians seeking care may be investigated; marker mismatch can trigger questioning or denial.
minors_guardians.protection: City schools add X; municipal/state nondiscrimination and care sanctuary protect local minors/parents; no adult or facility ban documented in division for youth care.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family exposure concentrates at border and in federally funded care/school programs; division protections may reduce local school/care encounters but not federal inquiries.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific visitor violence pattern documented; state hate-crime coverage absent; broad survey hostility and archaic morality laws create uncertain street risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State nondiscrimination commission awards damages/training; city ordinances bar service discrimination; legal-risk assessment places division low-risk for targeting adults.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police are more likely to respond via civil remedies, but federal or out-of-state hostility could affect severe incidents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal policies are evolving and partially litigated; pending state bills; enforcement variation at ports/federal facilities; whether sanctuary shields all visitors is unclear.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Local commission and city sanctuary offer prompt remedies; legal-aid FAQ and lawsuits mitigate document confusion; several federal orders have court blocks.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are strongest at state/city level and weakest at federal border/custody, so protection is patchy and dependent on setting.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-B because division nondiscrimination/sanctuary reduces routine stops/fines, but federal border confiscation/stranding and custody severity keep it below protective regimes.
Similar to 0.45-D: database/officer exposure at entry and facilities/funding restrictions. Local open documents and care sanctuary raise it slightly, while immigration-custody abuse lowers it.
Lower than 0.55-B because border admin mismatch can become fraud/lifetime ban and documented severe immigration custody, unlike mere return transport.
Much lower than 0.75-C; its border officers are trained and remedies work, while this federal regime actively restricts markers and facilities.

parsed.synthesis: Border is universal and harsh; once outed, federal authorities may deny entry or escalate fraud investigation into detention, where placement and abuse are documented. Within division, city/state nondiscrimination and sanctuary reduce everyday service, facility and adult-care harm. Federal facilities/funding, immigration custody, minors’ care rules and threat framing remain live constraints. Remedies are local mostly; federal legal challenges give uncertain relief. The resulting regime is not low risk, but protective division keeps it above purely federal-exclusion cases.
